name: weighted cycle crosses batch boundaries
test:
datasets = {'a': [10, 11, 12], 'b': [20, 21]}
batcher = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 2)
assert batcher.next_batch() == [('a', 10), ('a', 11)]
assert batcher.next_batch() == [('b', 20), ('a', 12)]

name: non-divisible batch size keeps global schedule
test:
datasets = {'a': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 'b': [9, 8, 7]}
batcher = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 4)
first = batcher.next_batch()
second = batcher.next_batch()
assert [name for name, _ in first] == ['a', 'a', 'b', 'a']
assert [name for name, _ in second] == ['a', 'b', 'a', 'a']

name: global offset skips dataset values
input: offset = 3 with schedule a, a, b

name: state resumes exact suffix
input: save after one batch and resume in a fresh instance
test:
datasets = {'a': [10, 11, 12], 'b': [20, 21]}
original = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 3)
original.next_batch()
state = original.state_dict()
expected = original.next_batch()
resumed = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 3).load_state_dict(state)
assert resumed.next_batch() == expected

name: short datasets cycle deterministically
input: dataset a has one item, dataset b has two items

name: invalid constructor arguments raise
input: empty datasets, missing weights, zero weight, non-positive batch size
test:
def must_raise(call):
    try:
        call()
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError('expected ValueError')

must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({}, {'a': 1}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'b': 1}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'a': 0}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': []}, {'a': 1}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'a': 1}, 0))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'a': 1}, 1, offset=-1))
